title: Daily Bread
subtitle: Thirty days. The rung everything else stands on.
note: Week 4 runs nine days (22-30), not seven. Do NOT compute week from day for this course - use each day's own week_number.

week_list.title: Show Up
week_list.opening_line: This is the easiest week of your life and roughly half of women do not finish it.
week_list.stakes: Skip it and you spend the next three weeks building on a base that is not there — and you will not find out until day twenty-four, which is the worst possible day to find out.
week_list.pull_quote: You are not starting a fitness program. You are finding out whether your own word means anything, and you already suspect it doesn't.

blocks.v: The four shapes

blocks.label: Hollow
blocks.cue: Low back flat to the floor, ribs down, head and feet lifted, held from the middle. Twenty seconds, twice.

blocks.label: Arch
blocks.cue: Chest and thighs lifted, throat open, chin up, the front of you unguarded. Twenty seconds, twice.

blocks.label: Stacked
blocks.cue: Standing under something. Head over ribs over hips over heels. Nothing shoved sideways. Thirty seconds each hand.

blocks.label: Landing
blocks.cue: Drop off a low step and land. Feet flat, knees soft, chest up, still for one second. Quiet feet. Five reps.

blocks.v: Two minutes. That is the whole drill. You will do it every day for thirty days and nothing gets added to it. On any day you miss the thirty minutes, you still do this.

blocks.title: The four shapes, and where they go next
rows: Hollow
In Strong and Surrendered it is under load. In The Honest Room it is what your body does when somebody says a true thing to you and you stay.
Arch
In Still Waters it is how you sit to pray. It is also the hardest one to do in front of another person and you will find that out.
Stacked
In Strong and Surrendered it is every carry. Everywhere else it is not performing.
Landing
In every program it is the same thing — you fell, and you are back the next morning without a speech.

blocks.v: Falling is routine

Read this now, while nothing has gone wrong. You will miss a day. Probably two. Every gymnast who ever learned a skill fell off it repeatedly, in public, and got back on it the same afternoon without a conversation about it.

left.head: What you will make it mean
items: I am not the kind of woman who finishes.
I will start again on the first of the month.

right.head: What it actually is
items: I moved the slot to the morning.

items.head: Mark the day you did
items.sub: Do not hide the gap. A blank is honest and a hidden blank is not.

items.head: Four words
items.sub: Post: missed one, back today. Exactly that. No reason — the reason is where the shame gets in.

items.head: Do the two minutes
items.sub: The four shapes happen on the day you fall. In whatever you are wearing. This is the landing and it is the actual skill.

items.head: Go the next morning
items.sub: Not a bigger session to make up for it. The ordinary one, at your time, as though nothing happened. Because nothing did.

items.head: Thirty minutes daily
items.sub: Your choice, your intensity, logged every night with the actual number on it.

items.head: The four shapes, two minutes
items.sub: All four, every day, before the thirty minutes. Never skipped.

items.head: One time of day, kept
items.sub: The same slot, seven days running. This is the week's real assignment and it is not the movement.

items.head: One written line, nightly
items.sub: One sentence. Not a diary entry.

blocks.title: The inner work — What You Promised in January

items.head: Ten minutes, on paper
items.sub: Every promise you have made to yourself about your body in the last five years. All of them. Do not think, list.

items.head: Beside each one
items.sub: How many days it lasted. A number, not a story.

items.head: Circle the longest one
items.sub: Not the best one. The one that ran longest before it stopped.

items.head: One line underneath
items.sub: What was happening on the day it stopped. Where you were standing. What you told yourself that night.

blocks.text: Whoever is faithful in very little is also faithful in much.
blocks.why: It is not a moral warning. It is a training principle, and it was written two thousand years before anybody wrote a progression chart.

blocks.title: When it doesn't work
rows: You did not pick a time of day
This is the corner, and it is the only one that matters this week. Everything downstream fails here. Go and pick one now, out loud, and write it in ink.
You did four big sessions instead of seven small ones
Four is not seven. Cut every session to thirty minutes and go every day. You are training a frequency, not a body, and the body comes free with it.
You skipped the shapes because the thirty minutes felt like enough
The two minutes are the non-negotiable and the thirty are the flexible part. You have it backwards, and week three is where that shows.
You are already bored
Good. Boring is what daily looks like from the inside, and the fact that you expected it to feel like something is the exact belief this month is dismantling.
You are ill, travelling, or in pain
Lie on the floor and breathe for thirty minutes. Log it as that. It counts identically and nobody is grading the content.

blocks.title: Not every hard thing is a cut corner
blocks.v: If the promises page brought up something bigger than a habit — old material arriving with your whole body attached — that is not a cut corner and I will not treat it as one. Keep the daily practice and take that to somebody licensed to hold it.

week_list.title: Keep It
week_list.opening_line: Week two is where you meet the voice that has ended every one of these before, and it is not going to sound like an enemy. It is going to sound extremely reasonable.
week_list.stakes: Skip the negotiation and you will believe, for another decade, that you are a woman who does not follow through — when what you actually are is a woman who has never once heard the sentence out loud.
week_list.pull_quote: You are not lazy and you are not broken. You have been having a negotiation every morning that you did not know was happening.

blocks.v: Thirty minutes of anything you chose on purpose stays exactly as it was. The base does not change. What goes on top of it does.

items.sub: Same as last week. Same time.

items.sub: Two sessions this week are harder than the same session last week. A hill, a heavier bag, five more minutes, one more round.

items.head: Carry something
items.sub: Once. Heavy enough that you would rather not, far enough that you have to change hands.

items.head: The four shapes, two minutes

items.head: Catch it in the act
items.sub: The morning it happens, stop and write the sentence down verbatim, in the voice it arrives in. Quotation marks.

items.head: Do not argue with it
items.sub: Not on paper, not in your head. You are collecting, not debating.

items.head: Collect three of them
items.sub: Over the week. Most women find the same one three times.

items.head: Read them back on day fourteen
items.sub: Out loud, standing, flat. That is the whole intervention and it works better than willpower.

blocks.title: When it doesn't work
rows: You retook the baseline numbers
Then they are not numbers, they are a performance, and in three weeks you will have nothing to compare against. Take them again cold on day nine and write the first attempt.
The negotiation never showed up in words
It is there and it is preverbal. Write what you did instead — the phone, the second coffee, the reorganised morning. The behaviour is the sentence.
You went heavier and now something hurts
Sharp, in a joint, one side only, still there tomorrow — that is pain and not effort. Stop that movement, take the range smaller, and go and see somebody with letters after their name.
You are logging but not writing
The written line is half the product. Sixty seconds. Do not upgrade it into journalling, just answer the question.
You missed a day
Four words, the two minutes, the ordinary session tomorrow. That is the entire protocol.

week_list.title: The Week You Miss
week_list.opening_line: I scheduled this week a year ago. If you have already fallen, you are on time.
week_list.stakes: Skip this and the first miss of the rest of your life ends the practice — because you will still be carrying a private rule that says a broken streak is a verdict, and you will never once have tested it.
week_list.pull_quote: Falling is not the interruption to the training. Falling is the training.

blocks.label: The landing
blocks.cue: Drop off a low step. Feet flat, knees soft, chest up, still for one second at the bottom. Quiet feet. Ten a day, every day this week, including any day you miss everything else.

blocks.title: Return time is the only number that matters
blocks.v: Not the length of the streak. Not the total days. The gap, in days, between falling off and getting back on. A woman with a return time of one day will still be training in ten years. A woman with a perfect streak and no return protocol is one bad Wednesday from stopping altogether, and she has no idea.

items.head: Ten landings, daily
items.sub: Added to the four shapes, all seven days, including any day you miss everything else.

items.head: Thirty minutes daily
items.sub: Unchanged. Same time.

items.head: One session with no mirror and no clock
items.sub: Cover the mirror. Leave the watch. Go by feel and find out how badly you need the instruments.

items.head: The four shapes
items.sub: Every day. Non-negotiable, and this is the week that phrase gets tested.

blocks.title: The inner work — The Return Plan

items.head: Write the four words now
items.sub: Missed one, back today. In the book, before you need it.

items.head: Name the likely day
items.sub: Look at your fourteen days. Which weekday is thinnest? That is the one coming for you.

items.head: Write what you will do at eleven at night
items.sub: Specifically. Which two minutes, in what room, in what clothes.

items.head: Write who you will tell
items.sub: One name, or the Circle. A restart that nobody sees is one you can quietly cancel.

blocks.title: Done means
items: Ten landings on all seven days, including any missed day

One session taken with no mirror, no clock and no numbers

blocks.demo: Say your return plan out loud from memory: the four words, the room, the clothes, and the name of the person you tell.

blocks.q: What do you do at eleven at night on a missed day?
Is your return plan written or intended?

blocks.title: When it doesn't work
rows: You have not fallen and you are treating that as the achievement
The streak is not the product. Write the return plan anyway, this week, while it is cheap. You are buying insurance and the premium goes up after the fire.
You fell and disappeared for four days
The falling was routine. The four days were the injury. Go back today, four words, no reason. Then write down what happened on day two that made day three easier to skip.
You posted the four words with a paragraph of explanation attached
The reason is where the shame gets in and a paragraph is an invitation to be forgiven. Four words. That is the whole discipline and it takes about nine seconds.
You cannot do the landings — knees, ankles, pelvic floor
Step down instead of dropping, off a stair, one leg at a time, and take the same one-second stillness at the bottom. The stillness is the skill and the height never was.
The no-mirror session made you anxious
That is the week working. Do it once more before Sunday and say nothing about it to anybody.

blocks.title: What is not a cut corner
blocks.v: If what surfaced on the missed day was old and it arrived with your whole body attached, that is not a cut corner and it does not get drilled at. Keep the practice. Take that part to a licensed professional.

week_list.title: Nine Days
week_list.opening_line: Nine days, not seven. You are past the part where this is impressive and into the part where it is simply what you do.
week_list.stakes: Skip these last nine and you will have spent a month proving something to yourself and then quit two days before the door opened — which is the specific way most women lose the thing they have already paid for.
week_list.pull_quote: Ask boldly. Prepare like it is coming. Then receive it without putting it down and running.

blocks.v: You cannot watch your own form. It was easy to change when somebody else saw it — easy, not brave. The seeing was the whole cost. The fixing was nothing. This is the week you let yourself be seen.

items.head: Load, twice

items.head: The compulsories, once

items.head: One long one
items.sub: Sixty minutes, conversational, day twenty-six. Longer than anything you have done this month.

items.head: The four shapes
items.sub: Every day. Nine of nine. Nothing added and nothing skipped.

items.head: Ten minutes, verbs only
items.sub: What do you want to be able to do. Not have, not feel, not look like. Do. No ranking and no crossing out.

items.head: Circle the one that tightened your chest
items.sub: Not the sensible one.

items.head: Write what you would have to become
items.sub: Four lines, no more. Capacities, not adjectives.

items.head: Pray it out loud, once, standing
items.sub: Named, specific, out loud, with your eyes open. God is for you and He is not vague. Neither should you be.

blocks.title: The eight compulsories
cols: Why it is on the list
rows: Floor and up
The one you lose first and notice last.
Kneel and rise
Every low cupboard, every child, every garden.
Lift something heavy
Off the ground, with your hips.
Carry it far
Groceries, water, a case, a child on a bad night.
Carry it up stairs
The one that decides whether you can live where you live.
Overhead onto a shelf
Shoulders that still go over your head at seventy-five.
Stand for a while
Four hours on your feet without your back deciding.
Walk
An hour, conversational, without planning around it.

blocks.q: What did you do the last time somebody said something good?

blocks.v: Which door
You have the thirty days. That is the gate on all three programs and you are through it. Choose while it is still in your body.

blocks.title: The three doors
rows: You want to be strong, and the mirror has been the enemy for thirty years
Strong and Surrendered. Eight weeks. Gymnastics progressions turned on a grown woman's whole life.
You cannot be still, you have downloaded three apps, and you read that as a discipline problem
Still Waters. Four weeks. Christian contemplative practice with a progression under it, because nobody ever gave you one.
You did the therapy, you can name the pattern in one clean sentence, and you are quietly furious that naming it changed nothing
The Honest Room. Ten weeks, twelve seats, application required, and completed clinical work is a hard prerequisite alongside the thirty days.
You are not ready to choose
Stay in the app. The count does not reset, the Circle stays, and the door is open whenever you want it.
You want to do it again
Do it again. Nobody in a gym finds a second cycle of the compulsories embarrassing. Second time through, take the numbers seriously and keep the same time of day.

blocks.title: When it doesn't work
rows: You cannot write a verb, only a feeling
Ask it differently. What could you do at thirty that you cannot do now, and which stairs would tell you. Concrete first, the feeling comes free.
You posted the tidy version
Everybody does, the first time. Post one more, today, and make it the thinnest day you have had this month. Nobody will do what you are afraid they will do.
You did not retake the numbers because you are afraid one went down

One probably did. Retake them anyway and write both columns. A number that went down in a month where you showed up twenty-nine times is telling you something useful and it is not about your character.
You are on day twenty-eight and quietly finished
This is the corner this week exists for. Two more. Ordinary ones. That is the entire remaining assignment.
